Legal draft

Privacy Policy

A structured privacy draft for review before public launch.

DRAFT — requires professional legal review.

Not attorney-approved. Final wording and organisation details must be approved before broad public launch.

The short version

This website does not access your company records. Its examples are fictional, and the enquiry preview does not send or store your details. The final privacy notice must explain how the separate application and its providers handle personal information.

For a practical explanation, read AI & Data Use. The full draft below still needs professional review.

Scope and responsible party

This draft covers the public O-IBS marketing website and identifies topics that the separate application privacy notice must address. The responsible legal entity, registration details, Information Officer and approved privacy contact have not yet been supplied.

Account and enquiry information

The final policy must describe account identifiers, contact details, company information and any enquiries processed through approved services. The current enquiry preview does not send or store the information entered. Do not include confidential financial information in a website enquiry.

Business, customer and supplier data

Application records may include invoices, payments and customer or supplier details. The final notice must identify which information the application processes, why, the applicable lawful grounds and the respective responsibilities of O-IBS and its business users. The marketing website does not connect to the application database.

Uploaded documents

The application notice must identify the handling of uploaded business documents, access boundaries, service providers, storage locations, retention and deletion. No upload function or document storage is provided by this public marketing site.

AI-assisted functionality

The final notice must explain which information is supplied to AI services, for which purposes, who provides those services, and the applicable retention and transfer arrangements. Website Bizzy demonstrations use synthetic examples only. Review uncertain AI-assisted information; business-changing actions require human confirmation.

Service providers and international transfers

Before publication, confirm the relevant hosting, email, storage and AI operators, their contractual roles and any cross-border processing arrangements. No list of providers or storage locations is asserted in this draft.

Cookies and website analytics

This website currently uses no advertising trackers, third-party fonts or analytics scripts and does not use browser storage for enquiries. Hosting request logs depend on the selected provider and must be covered by the final policy. If optional analytics or non-essential cookies are introduced, review the privacy notice and appropriate consent handling first.

Retention, deletion and safeguards

The final policy must set purpose-specific retention periods, deletion and backup handling, access controls and security arrangements. This draft does not promise an unverified retention period, encryption configuration or compliance certification.

Rights and contact requests

The approved policy must explain how people request access, correction or deletion, raise objections where applicable and verify their identity proportionately. Approved request channels and response procedures are still required. Use the Information Regulator’s official guidance for South African privacy information.

Approved contact details

An operational O-IBS privacy address has not been configured. Approved contact details and a request process will be added before release.

Official resources: Information Regulator — POPIA · Complaints information
